html: The Thiin, also called Tenma, were an Aboriginal Australian people of the southern Pilbara in Western Australia, in the country of the upper Ashburton and Henry rivers. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Their language is Thiinma. Little is recorded about them. Their neighbours included the Jiwarli and Jurruru to the north and west, the Warriyangga to the south and the Yinhawangka to the east. Sheep stations took up this country from the late 1800s.
